Finds harbor porpoise feeding buzzes

Source: R/fp_find_buzzes.R
fp_find_buzzes.Rd

This function uses one of two methods to classify NBHF clicks into one of two classes: feeding buzz or non feeding buzz.

Usage

fp_find_buzzes(x, method = "clicks", ...)

Arguments

x

a data.table where each row is a click, as the "clicks" element in the list object returned by fp_read(). Each row must minimally have a POSIXct column time, with nanosecond precision.

method

the method to use to find feeding buzzes. See details.

...

Additional arguments passed to specific methods, when relevant. For method="threshold", you can pass threshold=10 to define the maximum ICI for a buzz (with values interpreted in units of milliseconds)

Value

An integer vector of the same length as nrow(x), where the values indicate that that click (or a sequence of clicks) can be considered a feeding buzz (value = 1) or not (value = 0).

Details

Note that the so-called "feeding buzzes" are usually considered to represent a combination of feeding buzzes and social calls. Even so, the classifications resulting from all of these methods are commonly used as a proxy of foraging activity.

The available methods are:

  • clicks or pirotta1 method: any inter-click-interval (ICI) less than 20 milliseconds is considered a NBHF feeding buzz.

  • trains or pirotta2 method: buzzes are identified using a mixture Gaussian model, with the number of components k=3. All clicks associated with the first component are considered a NBHF feeding buzz. This method requires the package mixtools to work. Note that different implementations of this method sometimes use different units for the ICIs (e.g. decimal minutes or milliseconds). The choice of units doesn't necessarily change the estimates, but it may affect the numerical stability of the computation and lead to false/early/non-optimal convergence. Therefore, the fpod package uses units of milliseconds.

  • sbfi or sbfi1 method: the Search Buzz Foraging Identification method described in Aofui et al 2026. Requires 3 or more consecutive ICIs between 1.25 - 6.65 ms, preceded in the same minute by a search/approach click (< 200 clicks/s). Minute groups are pre-defined based on the FPOD starting time.

  • sbfi2 method: as sbfi, but with a small refinement. Rather than restrict the identification of search-buzzes to pre-defined minute groups, this method uses an adaptive minute window. It first identifies clusters of buzzes, and then identifies the subset of those clusters that are preceded by a search click within 60s (disregarding minute chunks). This method is more resilient to edge-cases, where you have a search-buzz sequence on either side of a minute (that would otherwise be missed with method="sbfi"). This affects absolute buzz numbers more than derived estimates such as buzz-positive-minutes. The latter isn't necessarily very different between these two variations of the SBFI. Note that buzzes for the edge cases always get assigned to the later minute.

  • threshold method: any inter-click-interval (ICI) less than the defined threshold is considered a NBHF feeding buzz. The threshold must be specified in milliseconds.

References

Aoufi, S., Rumes, B., Vanaverbeke, J., Degraer, S., & Debusschere, E. (2026). A Novel Method to Infer Harbor Porpoise Foraging Behavior From Acoustic Data: A Comparative Assessment Against Established Techniques. Marine Mammal Science, 42(4), e70292. https://doi.org/10.1111/mms.70292

Pirotta, E., Thompson, P.M., Miller, P.I., Brookes, K.L., Cheney, B., Barton, T.R., Graham, I.M. and Lusseau, D. (2014), Scale-dependent foraging ecology of a marine top predator modelled using passive acoustic data. Funct Ecol, 28: 206-217. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.12146

Examples

# first read some FPOD data
fn <- fp_example("gullars_period1.FP3")
dat <- fp_read(fn)

# extract porpoise clicks of quality Hi and Mod
nbhf <- dat$clicks[species == "NBHF" & quality_level >= 2]

# then add a 'feeding buzz' column to the clicks data.table
nbhf$pirotta1 <- fp_find_buzzes(nbhf, method = "clicks")

# using method="clicks" is the equivalent of this:
nbhf$threshold20ms <- fp_find_buzzes(nbhf, method = "threshold", threshold = 20)

# using the gaussian mixture model approach is just as easy:
nbhf$pirotta2 <- fp_find_buzzes(nbhf, method = "pirotta2")
#> number of iterations= 194 

# or we can use one of two variations of the SBFI
nbhf$sbfi <- fp_find_buzzes(nbhf, method = "sbfi")
nbhf$sbfi2 <- fp_find_buzzes(nbhf, method = "sbfi2")

# we can easily compare all of these methods in terms of absolute buzz
# numbers and positive buzz minutes (BPMs)

# first extract only the cols that we need to do this
buzz <- nbhf[, .(minute, pirotta1, threshold20ms, pirotta2, sbfi, sbfi2)]
# define BPMs
bpm <- buzz[, lapply(.SD, function(x) any(x>0)), by = minute][,-1]

# finally, print comparative table
data.frame(
    method = names(bpm),
    tot_clicks = nrow(nbhf),
    tot_buzzes = as.integer(buzz[,lapply(.SD,sum)][,-1]),
    bpm = as.integer(bpm[,lapply(.SD,sum)])
)
#>          method tot_clicks tot_buzzes bpm
#> 1      pirotta1      43216       8962 169
#> 2 threshold20ms      43216       8962 169
#> 3      pirotta2      43216       4752  79
#> 4          sbfi      43216       5204  64
#> 5         sbfi2      43216       5204  64
